options: are endonucleases which cleave DNA at specific sites
make DNA complementary to an existing DNA or RNA
are required in vectorless direct gene transfer.
1907.sol: Restriction enzymes are endonucleases which cleave DNA at specific sites. They are originally extracted from the bacterium E.coli. Type I restriction enzymes bind to a recognition site of a duplex DNA and cleave one strand only. Type II restriction enzymes are more valuable in gene manipulation and cleave the duplex at specific target sites at or near the binding site.

2346.subject: Chemistry
2346.text:
Identify $( Z )$ in the following reaction:

${CH}_{3}COOH\overset{{LiAlH}_{4}}{⟶} ( X ) \overset{Cu}{573K} ( Y ) \overset{dil . NaOH}{⟶}$$( Z )$
2346.sol:
${LiAlH}_{4}$ can reduce the carboxylic acid into the alcohol. So, the acetic acid is converted into the ethanol by ${LiAlH}_{4}$ in reaction $X$. Copper is an oxidising agent. It can oxidise the alcohol to the aldehyde. So, it oxidises the ethanol to the ethanal in reaction $Y$.

The ethanal has the alpha hydrogen. So, the weak base will take the acidic hydrogen. It will form the carbanion. After that the carbanion will give the nucleophilic addition reaction with another mole of ethanal. The $\beta$-hydroxylcarbonyl compound is formed as a product.

Reaction :-

${CH}_{3}COOH\overset{{LiAlH}_{4}}{⟶}{CH}_{3}{CH}_{2}OH\mathop{\to}_{573K}^{Cu}{CH}_{3}CHO\overset{dil . NaOH}{⟶}{CH}_{3} - CH ( OH ) - {CH}_{2} - CHO ( Aldol )$

Hence the $Z$ in this reaction is aldol.

3569.text: What is the correct order of spin only magnetic moment (in BM) of $\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}, \mathrm{Cr}^{2+}$ and $\mathrm{V}^{2+}$ ?
3569.sol:
Spin only magnetic moments depend upon the number of unpaired electrons, more the number of unpaired electron, greater will be the spin only magnetic moment. ${ }_{25} \mathrm{Mn}=1 s^2, 2 s^2 2 p^6, 3 s^2 3 p^6 3 d^5, 4 s^2\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}=1 s^2, 2 s^2 2 p^6 3 s^2 3 p^6 3 d^5, 4 s^0$

Due to platinum electrodes, self ionization of water will take place.
$\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \rightarrow 2 \mathrm{H}^{+}+\mathrm{OH}^{-}$
At cathode: $2 \mathrm{H}^{+}+2 \mathrm{e}-\rightarrow \mathrm{H}_2$
At anode: $\mathrm{OH} \rightarrow 2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}+\mathrm{O}_2+4 \mathrm{e}$
Due to lower electrode potentials, $\mathrm{H}_2$ gas will generate at cathode and $\mathrm{O}_2$ gas will generate at anode.

When a non-volatile solute is added to a volatile solvent, the solute covers up some of the surface of solvent. Thus, less surface area is available for vaporisation of solvent and hence, vapour pressure decreases. As the amount of non-volatile solute increases, vapour pressure decreases accordingly.
$\because$ The order of concentration of $X$ is
$0.01 < 0.10 < 0.25\therefore$ The order of vapour pressure is
$p_3 > p_1 > p_2$

5345.subject: Chemistry
5345.text: Which among the following is a unitless physical quantity?
5345.sol: Mole fraction is a unit of concentration, defined to be equal to the number of moles of a component divided by the total number of moles of a solution. Because it is a ratio, mole fraction is a unitless expression. The mole fraction of all components of a solution, when added together, will equal 1. Hence, the correct option is (3).

5598.subject: Chemistry
5598.text:
The wavelength associated with the electron moving in the first orbit of hydrogen atom with velocity $2.2 \times 10^6 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$ (in nm) is
$\left(m_e=9.0 \times 10^{-31} \mathrm{~kg}, h=6.6 \times 10^{-34} \mathrm{Js}\right)$
5598.sol:
According to de-Broglie's equation,
$\lambda=\frac{h}{m v}$
where, $\lambda$ is wavelength
$h$ is Planck's constant $\left(6.626 \times 10^{-34} \mathrm{Js}\right)m$ is mass of electron (given $9.0 \times 10^{-31} \mathrm{~kg}$ )
$v$ is velocity of electron (given $2.2 \times 10^6 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ )
$\therefore \quad \lambda=\frac{6.626 \times 10^{-34}}{9.0 \times 10^{-31} \times 2.2 \times 10^6}=0.33 \times 10^{-9} \mathrm{~m}$
i.e. $0.33 \mathrm{~nm}$ (as $1 \mathrm{~nm}=10^{-9} \mathrm{~m}$ )

7634.text: If $f: R \rightarrow R$ is defined by $f(x)=x-[x]$, where $[x]$ is the greatest integer not exceeding $x$, then the set of discontinuous of $f$ is
7634.sol:
We know that,
$$
f(x)=\left\{\begin{array}{cc}
x-(n-1) & \text{ for }-1 < x < n \\
0 & \text{ for } x=n \\
x-n & \text{ for } n < x < n+1
\end{array}\right.
$$
where $n \in z$
Now, we check the continuity at $x=n$
$$
\begin{aligned}
f(n-0) & =\lim _{x \rightarrow n^{-}}[x-(n-1)] \\
& =\lim _{h \rightarrow 0}[n-h-n+1) \\
& =1 \\
f(n+0) & =\lim _{x \rightarrow n^{+}}[x-n] \\
& =\lim _{h \rightarrow 0}(n+h-n)=0
\end{aligned}
$$
and
$$
f(n)=0
$$
$\Rightarrow f(x)$ is discontinuous at $x=n$
$\therefore$ Set of discontinuous of $f$ is $z$

12174.text: If the coordinates of a point $P$ changes to $(2,-6)$ when the coordinate axes are rotated through an angle of $135^{{}^{\circ}}$, then the coordinates of $P$ in the original system are
12174.sol:
If $(x, y)$ is old coordinates and $(X, Y)$ are new coordinates, when axes are rotated through an angle of $\theta$, then $\begin{aligned}& x=X \cos \theta- Y \sin \theta \text{$ and $} y=X \sin \theta+ Y \cos \theta\\
& \therefore \quad x=2 \cos 135^{{}^{\circ}}-(-6) \sin 135^{{}^{\circ}} \\
& \text{ and } \quad y=2 \sin 135^{{}^{\circ}}+(-6) \cos 135^{{}^{\circ}} \\
& \Rightarrow x=2\left(\frac{-1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)+6\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right) \text{ and } y=2\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)-6\left(\frac{-1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)\\
& \Rightarrow x=\frac{4}{\sqrt{2}} \text{ and } y=\frac{8}{\sqrt{2}}\\
& \Rightarrow x=2 \sqrt{2} \text{ and } y=4 \sqrt{2} .
\end{aligned}\therefore$ Coordinates of $P$ in the original system are $(2 \sqrt{2}, 4 \sqrt{2})$.

12874.text: The range of $\frac{1}{\sin ^2 x+3 \sin x \cos x+5 \cos ^2 x}$ is
12874.sol:
$\begin{aligned} & \text{Let } f(x)=\frac{1}{\sin ^2 x+3 \sin x \cos x+5 \cos ^2 x} \\ & \text{ let, } g(x)=\sin ^2 x+3 \sin x \cos x+5 \cos ^2 x \\ & =2[1+\cos 2 \theta]+1+\frac{3}{2} \sin 2 \theta \\ & g(x)=\frac{3}{2} \sin 2 \theta+2 \cos 2 \theta+3\end{aligned}$
We know the minimum and maximum value of $a \sin x+b \cos x+c$ are $c-\sqrt{a^2+b^2}$ and $c+\sqrt{a^2+b^2}$ respectively.
$\therefore$ Min. value of $g(x)=3-\sqrt{\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^2+(2)^2}=3-\frac{5}{2}=\frac{1}{2}$
and max. value of $g(x)=3+\sqrt{\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^2+(2)^2}=3+\frac{5}{2}=\frac{11}{2}$
Min. value of $f(x)=\frac{1}{\text{ Max. value of } g(x)}=\frac{1}{\frac{11}{2}}=\frac{2}{11}$
Max. value of $f(x)=\frac{1}{\text{ Min. value of } g(x)}=\frac{1}{\frac{1}{2}}=2\therefore \quad$ Range of $f(x)=\frac{1}{\sin ^2 x+3 \sin x \cos x+5 \cos ^2 x}$ is $\left[\frac{2}{11}, 2\right]$

Average speed $=\frac{\text{ Total distance }}{\text{ Time taken }}$

Now, a car C is moving in the opposite direction let's& say with velocity& ${v}_{C}$ then, the relative velocity of car C with respect to A and B is ${v}_{CB} = {v}_{CA} = {v}_{C} - {v}_{A}$

Given that distance of separation between cars A and B is $10$ kmand speed of cars is $30kmph$

Also, given that car C crossed B& and A& in& $8min\text{or}\dfrac{8}{60}hrs$ then, it means that car C travels a distance of $10$ kmin $\dfrac{2}{15}hrs$ with relative velocity ${v}_{CA}$

$\text{Distance = speed \times time} ⇒ 10km = {v}_{CA} \times \dfrac{2}{15}hrs ⇒ {v}_{CA} = 75kmph ⇒ {v}_{C} - {v}_{A} = 75kmph ⇒ {v}_{C} = 75 + {v}_{A} ⇒ {v}_{C} = 75 + \left(- 30\right) = 45kmph$

20635.subject: Chemistry
20635.text: Lead storage battery contains $4.25 \mathrm{M}\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4$ which has a density of $1.24 \mathrm{ g} / \mathrm{ml}$. Calculate the molality of aqueous solution of $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4$.
20635.sol:
Given molarity $M = 4.25 \text{ mol/L}$ and density $d = 1.24 \text{ g/mL}$.

The molar mass of $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ is $2 \times 1 + 32 + 4 \times 16 = 98 \text{ g/mol}$.

Consider $1 \text{ L}$ of the solution. The mass of the solution is $1000 \text{ mL} \times 1.24 \text{ g/mL} = 1240 \text{ g}$.

The mass of the solute ($\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$) in $1 \text{ L}$ is $4.25 \text{ mol} \times 98 \text{ g/mol} = 416.5 \text{ g}$.

The mass of the solvent (water) is $1240 \text{ g} - 416.5 \text{ g} = 823.5 \text{ g} = 0.8235 \text{ kg}$.

Molality $m$ is defined as the number of moles of solute per kilogram of solvent:

$m = \dfrac{\text{moles of solute}}{\text{mass of solvent in kg}} = \dfrac{4.25}{0.8235} \approx 5.161 \text{ mol/kg}$.

Answer: $5.161$

20702.subject: Chemistry
20702.text:
If X is a haloalkane with a single Chlorine atom per molecule and the percentage of Cl is 55 , what would be the number of Cl atoms present in 0.1 g of the haloalkane?
Atomic mass of $\mathrm{Cl}=35.5 \mathrm{ g} / \mathrm{mol}$
20702.sol:
Let the molar mass of the haloalkane be $M$ g/mol. The percentage of Chlorine is given as $55\%$.

Since there is one Chlorine atom per molecule, the mass of Chlorine in one mole of the haloalkane is $35.5$ g. Therefore, $\dfrac{35.5}{M} \times 100 = 55$.

$M = \dfrac{35.5 \times 100}{55} = \dfrac{3550}{55} \approx 64.545$ g/mol.

The number of moles of the haloalkane in $0.1$ g is $n = \dfrac{0.1}{64.545} \approx 0.001549$ moles.

Since each molecule contains one Chlorine atom, the number of moles of Chlorine atoms is equal to the number of moles of the haloalkane, which is $0.001549$ moles.

The number of Chlorine atoms is $N = n \times N_{A} = 0.001549 \times 6.022 \times 10^{23} \approx 9.328 \times 10^{20}$.

Answer: $9.328 \times 10^{20}$

21089.subject: Mathematics
21089.text: The total number of terms in the expansion of $(x+y)^{60}+(x-y)^{60}$ is
21089.sol:
The expansion of $(x+y)^{n}$ is given by $\sum_{k=0}^{n} {^{n}C_{k}} x^{n-k} y^{k}$.

The expansion of $(x+y)^{60}$ is ${^{60}C_{0}} x^{60} + {^{60}C_{1}} x^{59} y + {^{60}C_{2}} x^{58} y^2 + \dots + {^{60}C_{60}} y^{60}$.

The expansion of $(x-y)^{60}$ is ${^{60}C_{0}} x^{60} - {^{60}C_{1}} x^{59} y + {^{60}C_{2}} x^{58} y^2 - \dots + {^{60}C_{60}} y^{60}$.

Adding these two expressions, the terms with odd powers of $y$ cancel out:

$(x+y)^{60} + (x-y)^{60} = 2 \left[ {^{60}C_{0}} x^{60} + {^{60}C_{2}} x^{58} y^2 + {^{60}C_{4}} x^{56} y^4 + \dots + {^{60}C_{60}} y^{60} \right]$.

The terms remaining correspond to $k = 0, 2, 4, \dots, 60$.

The number of such terms is $\dfrac{60 - 0}{2} + 1 = 30 + 1 = 31$.

Answer: 31

21428.subject: Mathematics
21428.text: If the distance between the foci is equal to the length of the latus rectum, then the eccentricity of the ellipse is
21428.sol:
For an ellipse with semi-major axis $a$ and semi-minor axis $b$, the distance between the foci is $2ae$ and the length of the latus rectum is $\dfrac{2b^2}{a}$.

Given that the distance between the foci is equal to the length of the latus rectum, we have $2ae = \dfrac{2b^2}{a}$.

Simplifying this, $ae = \dfrac{b^2}{a}$, which implies $a^2e = b^2$.

Using the relation $b^2 = a^2(1 - e^2)$, we substitute $b^2$ into the equation:

$a^2e = a^2(1 - e^2)$

$e = 1 - e^2$

$e^2 + e - 1 = 0$

Solving this quadratic equation for $e$ using the quadratic formula $e = \dfrac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}$:

$e = \dfrac{-1 \pm \sqrt{1^2 - 4(1)(-1)}}{2(1)} = \dfrac{-1 \pm \sqrt{5}}{2}$

Since the eccentricity $e$ must be positive for an ellipse, we take the positive root:

$e = \dfrac{\sqrt{5} - 1}{2}$

Answer: $\dfrac{\sqrt{5}-1}{2}$

21546.subject: Mathematics
21546.text: An unbiased die is tossed twice. What is the probability of getting a 4,5 or 6 on the first toss and a 1,2,3 or 4 on the second toss?
21546.sol:
The sample space for tossing an unbiased die twice consists of $6 \times 6 = 36$ equally likely outcomes.

Let $A$ be the event of getting a 4, 5, or 6 on the first toss. The number of favorable outcomes for the first toss is 3, so $P(A) = \dfrac{3}{6} = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

Let $B$ be the event of getting a 1, 2, 3, or 4 on the second toss. The number of favorable outcomes for the second toss is 4, so $P(B) = \dfrac{4}{6} = \dfrac{2}{3}$.

Since the two tosses are independent events, the probability of both events occurring is $P(A \cap B) = P(A) \times P(B)$.

$P(A \cap B) = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{2}{3} = \dfrac{1}{3}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{3}$

21997.subject: Mathematics
21997.text: A number consists of three digits in geometric progression. The sum of the right hand and left hand digits exceeds twice the middle digit by 1 and the sum of left hand and middle digits is two third of the sum of the middle and right hand digits. Then the sum of digits of number is
21997.sol:
Let the three digits of the number be $a/r$, $a$, and $ar$, where $r$ is the common ratio. Since these are digits, $a/r, a, ar \in \{0, 1, 2, ..., 9\}$.

The first condition states that the sum of the right hand and left hand digits exceeds twice the middle digit by 1:
$\dfrac{a}{r} + ar = 2a + 1$

The second condition states that the sum of the left hand and middle digits is two-thirds of the sum of the middle and right hand digits:
$\dfrac{a}{r} + a = \dfrac{2}{3}(a + ar)$

From the second equation, dividing by $a$ (assuming $a \neq 0$):
$\dfrac{1}{r} + 1 = \dfrac{2}{3}(1 + r)$
$\dfrac{1+r}{r} = \dfrac{2(1+r)}{3}$
Since $r \neq -1$ (as digits are positive), we have $\dfrac{1}{r} = \dfrac{2}{3}$, which gives $r = \dfrac{3}{2}$.

Substituting $r = \dfrac{3}{2}$ into the first equation:
$\dfrac{a}{3/2} + a(\dfrac{3}{2}) = 2a + 1$
$\dfrac{2a}{3} + \dfrac{3a}{2} = 2a + 1$
Multiplying by 6 to clear denominators:
$4a + 9a = 12a + 6$
$13a = 12a + 6$
$a = 6$.

The digits are $\dfrac{6}{3/2} = 4$, $6$, and $6 \times \dfrac{3}{2} = 9$.
The digits are $4, 6, 9$.

The sum of the digits is $4 + 6 + 9 = 19$.

Answer: 19

22056.subject: Mathematics
22056.text: $\text{ If } A=\{1,2,3,4,5\} \text{ and } B=\{2,3,6,7\} \text{ then number of elements in the set }(A \times B) \cap(B \times A) \text{$ is equal to }
22056.sol:
The set $A \times B$ consists of all ordered pairs $(a, b)$ where $a \in A$ and $b \in B$.

The set $B \times A$ consists of all ordered pairs $(b, a)$ where $b \in B$ and $a \in A$.

An element $(x, y)$ belongs to $(A \times B) \cap (B \times A)$ if and only if $(x, y) \in A \times B$ and $(x, y) \in B \times A$.

This implies $x \in A$, $y \in B$, $x \in B$, and $y \in A$.

Therefore, $x \in A \cap B$ and $y \in A \cap B$.

Given $A = \{1, 2, 3, 4, 5\}$ and $B = \{2, 3, 6, 7\}$, the intersection $A \cap B = \{2, 3\}$.

The number of elements in $A \cap B$ is $n(A \cap B) = 2$.

The set $(A \times B) \cap (B \times A)$ is equivalent to $(A \cap B) \times (A \cap B)$.

The number of elements is $n((A \cap B) \times (A \cap B)) = n(A \cap B) \times n(A \cap B) = 2 \times 2 = 4$.

Answer: 4

The original variance of the observations is $16$.

Therefore, the new standard deviation remains $4$.

Answer: $4$

22108.text: If the line $(3 x+14 y+7)+k(5 x+7 y+6)=0$ is perpendicular to $x$-axis then the value of ' $k$ ' is

The given equation of the line is $(3x + 14y + 7) + k(5x + 7y + 6) = 0$.

Rearranging the terms to group $x$ and $y$ coefficients:

$(3 + 5k)x + (14 + 7k)y + (7 + 6k) = 0$.

A line is perpendicular to the $x$-axis if it is a vertical line, which means the coefficient of $y$ must be zero and the coefficient of $x$ must be non-zero.

Setting the coefficient of $y$ to zero:

$14 + 7k = 0$.

$7k = -14$.

$k = -2$.

Checking the coefficient of $x$ for $k = -2$:

$3 + 5(-2) = 3 - 10 = -7$, which is not zero. Thus, the line is indeed vertical.

Answer: $-2$

22940.text: A gas bubble of volume $2 \mathrm{ cm}^3$ rises from the bottom of a pond of depth 10 m at $17^0 \mathrm{C}$. What will be the volume of the bubble when it reaches the surface of the pond? Atmospheric temperature is $27^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$ and the pressure at the bottom of the pond is double that of the pressure at the surface.
22940.sol:
Let $P_1$ and $V_1$ be the pressure and volume at the bottom of the pond, and $P_2$ and $V_2$ be the pressure and volume at the surface. Given $V_1 = 2 \text{ cm}^3$.

The temperature at the bottom is $T_1 = 17 + 273 = 290 \text{ K}$. The temperature at the surface is $T_2 = 27 + 273 = 300 \text{ K}$.

The pressure at the bottom is given as double the atmospheric pressure, so $P_1 = 2P_2$.

Using the ideal gas law in the form $\dfrac{P_1 V_1}{T_1} = \dfrac{P_2 V_2}{T_2}$, we substitute the known values:

$\dfrac{2P_2 \times 2}{290} = \dfrac{P_2 \times V_2}{300}$

Canceling $P_2$ from both sides:

$\dfrac{4}{290} = \dfrac{V_2}{300}$

$V_2 = \dfrac{4 \times 300}{290} = \dfrac{1200}{290} \approx 4.137 \text{ cm}^3$.

Rounding to the nearest value provided in the options, we get $4.1 \text{ cm}^3$.

Answer: $4.1 \mathrm{ cm}^3$

Since both $12x$ and $2x$ lie in the first quadrant, $\sin(12x) > 0$ and $\sin(2x) > 0$.
Thus, $f(x) > 0$. This statement is true.

For option (c):
$f\left(x + \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) = \sin\left(12\left(x + \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\right)\sin\left(2\left(x + \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\right)$

$f\left(x + \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) = \sin(12x + 6\pi)\sin(2x + \pi)$

$f\left(x + \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) = \sin(12x)(-\sin(2x)) = -f(x)$

Therefore, $f\left(x + \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) + f(x) = 0$. This statement is true.

For option (d):
$f\left(\dfrac{\pi}{12}\right) = \sin\left(12 \times \dfrac{\pi}{12}\right)\sin\left(2 \times \dfrac{\pi}{12}\right) = \sin(\pi)\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) = 0 \times \dfrac{1}{2} = 0$. This statement is true.

For option (a):
At $x = \dfrac{3\pi}{2}$, $f\left(\dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right) = \sin(18\pi)\sin(3\pi) = 0$.
At $x = 2\pi$, $f(2\pi) = \sin(24\pi)\sin(4\pi) = 0$.
Since $f\left(\dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right) = f(2\pi) = 0$ and $f(x)$ is not a constant zero function, by Rolle's Theorem, $f'(x)$ must be zero at least once in the interval $\left(\dfrac{3\pi}{2}, 2\pi\right)$.
Hence, $f(x)$ cannot be strictly increasing on the entire interval $\left(\dfrac{3\pi}{2}, 2\pi\right)$. This statement is NOT true.

Answer: $f$ is increasing on $\left(\dfrac{3\pi}{2}, 2\pi\right)$.

25293.text: Let $a$ and $b$ be two nonzero real numbers. If the coefficient of ${x}^{5}$ in the expansion of ${\left(a{x}^{2} + \dfrac{70}{27bx}\right)}^{4}$ is equal to the coefficient of ${x}^{- 5}$ in the expansion of ${\left(ax - \dfrac{1}{b{x}^{2}}\right)}^{7}$, then the value of $2b$ is
25293.sol:
Given,

The coefficient of ${x}^{5}$ in ${\left(a{x}^{2} + \dfrac{70}{27bx}\right)}^{4}$ is equal to coefficient of ${x}^{- 5}$ in ${\left(ax - \dfrac{1}{b{x}^{2}}\right)}^{7}$,

Now finding the coefficient of ${x}^{5}$ in ${\left(a{x}^{2} + \dfrac{70}{27bx}\right)}^{4}$ we get,

${T}_{r + 1} = Cr 4 {\left(a{x}^{2}\right)}^{4 - r} \cdot {\left(\dfrac{70}{27bx}\right)}^{r}$

$⇒ {T}_{r + 1} = Cr 4 {\left(a\right)}^{4 - r} \cdot {\left(\dfrac{70}{27b}\right)}^{r} \cdot {x}^{8 - 2r - r}$

So, $8 - 2r - r = 5 ⇒ r = 1$

So, ${T}_{2} = C1 4 {a}^{3} \cdot \dfrac{70}{27b} \cdot {x}^{5}$

Now finding the coefficient of ${x}^{- 5}$ in ${\left(ax - \dfrac{1}{b{x}^{2}}\right)}^{7}$ we get,

${T}_{r + 1} = Cr 7 {\left(ax\right)}^{7 - r} \cdot {\left(\dfrac{1}{b{x}^{2}}\right)}^{r}$

$⇒ {T}_{r + 1} = Cr 7 {\left(a\right)}^{7 - r} \cdot {\left(\dfrac{1}{b}\right)}^{r} \cdot {x}^{7 - r - 2r}$

So, $7 - r - 2r = - 5 ⇒ r = 4$

So, ${T}_{5} = C4 7 {\left(a\right)}^{3} \cdot {\left(\dfrac{1}{b}\right)}^{4} \cdot {x}^{- 5}$

Now equating the coefficient of ${x}^{5} \text{ and } {x}^{- 5}$ we get,

$C4 7 {\left(a\right)}^{3} \cdot {\left(\dfrac{1}{b}\right)}^{4} = C1 4 {a}^{3} \cdot \dfrac{70}{27b}$

$⇒ 35{a}^{3} \cdot {\left(\dfrac{1}{b}\right)}^{4} = 4{a}^{3} \cdot \dfrac{70}{27b}$

$⇒ {\left(\dfrac{1}{b}\right)}^{3} = 4 \times \dfrac{2}{27}$

$⇒ b = \dfrac{3}{2} ⇒ 2b = 3$

26481.text: The center of a disk of radius $r$ and mass $m$ is attached to a spring of spring constant $k$, inside a ring of radius $R>r$ as shown in the figure. The other end of the spring is attached on the periphery of the ring. Both the ring and the disk are in the same vertical plane. The disk can only roll along the inside periphery of the ring, without slipping. The spring can only be stretched or compressed along the periphery of the ring, following the Hooke's law. In equilibrium, the disk is at the bottom of the ring. Assuming small displacement of the disc, the time period of oscillation of center of mass of the disk is written as $T=\frac{2 \pi}{\omega}$. The correct expression for $\omega$ is ( $g$ is the acceleration due to gravity):
26481.sol:
$E=\frac{1}{2} k(R-r)^2 \theta^2+m g(R-r)(1-\cos \theta)+\frac{1}{2} m v^2+\frac{1}{2} \frac{m r^2}{2} \omega^2$ Differentiating wrt t , $\begin{aligned} 0 & =\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{k}(\mathrm{R}-\mathrm{r})^2 \cdot 2 \theta \frac{\mathrm{~d} \theta}{\mathrm{dt}}+\mathrm{mg}(\mathrm{R}-\mathrm{r}) \cdot \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{dt}}\left(2 \frac{\theta^2}{4}\right)+\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{~m} \cdot 2 \mathrm{v} \frac{\mathrm{dv}}{\mathrm{dt}}+\frac{\mathrm{mr}^2}{4} \cdot 2 \omega \frac{\mathrm{~d} \omega}{\mathrm{dt}} \\ \Rightarrow & 0=\mathrm{k}(\mathrm{R}-\mathrm{r})^2 \theta \frac{\mathrm{~d} \theta}{\mathrm{dt}}+\mathrm{mg}(\mathrm{R}-\mathrm{r}) \theta \frac{\mathrm{d} \theta}{\mathrm{dt}}+\mathrm{mv} \frac{\mathrm{dv}}{\mathrm{dt}}+\frac{\mathrm{mr}^2}{2} \omega \frac{\mathrm{~d} \omega}{\mathrm{dt}}\end{aligned}$ Also, $\frac{d \theta}{d t}=\frac{V}{(R-r)} \Rightarrow \frac{d^2 \theta}{d t^2}=\frac{1}{(R-r)} \frac{d v}{d t}=\frac{1}{R-r} a \begin{aligned} & \therefore \mathrm{k}(\mathrm{R}-\mathrm{r})^2 \cdot \theta \frac{\mathrm{~V}}{\mathrm{R}-\mathrm{r}}+\mathrm{mg}(\mathrm{R}-\mathrm{r}) \theta \frac{\mathrm{V}}{\mathrm{R}-\mathrm{r}}=-\mathrm{mv} \alpha \mathrm{r}-\frac{\mathrm{mr}^2}{2} \frac{\mathrm{~V}}{\mathrm{r}} \alpha \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{k}(\mathrm{R}-\mathrm{r})+\mathrm{mg} \theta=-\frac{3}{2} \mathrm{mr} \alpha \\ & \Rightarrow-[\mathrm{k}(\mathrm{R}-\mathrm{r})+\mathrm{mg}] \theta=\frac{3}{2} \mathrm{~m}(\mathrm{R}-\mathrm{r}) \frac{\mathrm{d}^2 \theta}{\mathrm{dt}^2} \\ & \Rightarrow-\frac{2}{3}\left[\frac{\mathrm{k}}{\mathrm{m}}+\frac{\mathrm{g}}{\mathrm{R}-\mathrm{r}}\right]=\frac{\mathrm{d}^2 \theta}{\mathrm{dt}^2}\end{aligned}$ Compering with standard equation of SHM $\omega=\sqrt{\frac{2}{3}\left[\frac{\mathrm{k}}{\mathrm{m}}+\frac{\mathrm{g}}{\mathrm{R}-\mathrm{r}}\right]}$ Hence answer is option(A) $\mathrm{OR}$
$\mathrm{kx}+\mathrm{mg} \sin \theta-\mathrm{f}=\mathrm{ma} \begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \mathrm{kx}+\mathrm{mg} \frac{\mathrm{x}}{(\mathrm{R}-\mathrm{r})}-\mathrm{f}=\mathrm{ma} \\ & \mathrm{fr}=\frac{\mathrm{mr}^2}{2} \cdot \alpha \Rightarrow \mathrm{f}=\frac{\mathrm{ma}}{2} \\ & \therefore\left(\alpha+\frac{\mathrm{mg}}{\mathrm{R}-\mathrm{r}}\right) \mathrm{x}=\frac{3 \mathrm{ma}}{2} \\ & \therefore \omega=\sqrt{\frac{2}{3}\left[\frac{\mathrm{k}}{\mathrm{m}}+\frac{\mathrm{g}}{\mathrm{R}-\mathrm{r}}\right]}\end{aligned}$

27822.text:
Order of Covalent bond;

A. $KF > KI; LiF > KF$

B. $KF KF$

C. ${SnCl}_{4} > {SnCl}_{2}; CuCl > NaCl$

D. $LiF > KF; CuCl > NaCl$

E. $KF NaCl$
27822.sol:
According to Fajan's Rule, small cation has more polarising power and larger anion has more polarisability. These small cations and larger anions favours covalent character.

A. $KF > KI$$-$False (Iodide is larger anion than fluoride)

$LiF > KF -$True (Lithium-ion is smaller cation than potassium ion)

B. $KF < KI -$True; $LiF > KF -$True

C. ${SnCl}_{4} > {SnCl}_{2} -$True(${Sn}^{4 +}$ is smaller than ${Sn}^{2 +}$);

The ions with pseudo inert gas configuration prefers the covalent character.

$CuCl > NaCl -$True(${Cu}^{+} ( 3{s}^{2}3{p}^{6}3{d}^{10} )$ ion has pseudo inert gas configuration)

D. $LiF > KF -$True; $CuCl < NaCl -$False

E. $KF < KI -$True; $CuCl > NaCl -$True

33376.text: Let the coefficients of three consecutive terms in the binomial expansion of $( 1 + 2x{)}^{n}$ be in the ratio $2: 5: 8$. Then the coefficient of the term, which is in the middle of these three terms, is
33376.sol:
Given,

The coefficients of three consecutive terms in the binomial expansion of $( 1 + 2x{)}^{n}$ be in the ratio $2: 5: 8$.

Now ${r}^{th}$ term in expansion of $( 1 + 2x{)}^{n}$ is given by, ${t}_{r + 1} = Cr n ( 2x{)}^{r}$

Now let ${T}_{r}, {T}_{r + 1}, {T}_{r + 2}$ are in the ratio $2: 5: 8$

$⇒ \dfrac{{T}_{r}}{{T}_{r + 1}} = \dfrac{Cr - 1 n ( 2{)}^{r - 1}}{Cr n ( 2{)}^{r}} = \dfrac{2}{5}$

$⇒ \dfrac{\dfrac{n !}{( r - 1 ) ! ( n - r + 1 ) !}}{\dfrac{n ! ( 2 )}{r ! ( n - r ) !}} = \dfrac{2}{5}$

$⇒ \dfrac{r}{n - r + 1} = \dfrac{4}{5} ⇒ 5r = 4n - 4r + 4$

$⇒ 9r = 4 ( n + 1 ) . . . . . . . \left(1\right)$

Now taking other ratio $\dfrac{{T}_{r + 1}}{{T}_{r + 2}} = \dfrac{Cr n ( 2{)}^{r}}{Cr + 1 n ( 2{)}^{r + 1}} = \dfrac{5}{8}$

$⇒ \dfrac{\dfrac{n !}{r ! ( n - r ) !}}{\dfrac{n !}{( r + 1 ) ! ( n - r - 1 ) !}} = \dfrac{5}{4} ⇒ \dfrac{r + 1}{n - r} = \dfrac{5}{4}$

$⇒ 4r + 4 = 5n - 5r$

$⇒ 5n - 4 = 9r . . . . . . . . . \left(2\right)$

From equation $\left(1\right) \text{ and } \left(2\right)$ we get,

$4n + 4 = 5n - 4 ⇒ n = 8$ and $r = 4$

So, coefficient of middle term will be

$C4 8 {2}^{4} = 16 \times \dfrac{8 \times 7 \times 6 \times 5}{4 \times 3 \times 2 \times 1} = 16 \times 70 = 1120$

33626.text: Let the lines $y + 2x = \sqrt{11} + 7\sqrt{7}$ and $2y + x = 2\sqrt{11} + 6\sqrt{7}$ be normal to a circle $C: {\left(x - h\right)}^{2} + {\left(y - k\right)}^{2} = {r}^{2}$. If the line $\sqrt{11}y - 3x = \dfrac{5\sqrt{77}}{3} + 11$ is tangent to the circle $C$, then the value of ${\left(5h - 8k\right)}^{2} + 5{r}^{2}$ is equal to ______.

The equation of tangent is $\sqrt{11}y - 3x = \dfrac{5\sqrt{77}}{3} + 11$

The radius will be perpendicular distance of tangent from center

Hence ${\left(5h - 8k\right)}^{2} + 5{r}^{2} = 816$

33670.subject: Mathematics
33670.text: The locus of the centres of the circles, which touch the circle, ${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} = 1$ externally, also touch the $y$-axis and lie in the first quadrant, is:
33670.sol:
Let, the centre of the circle whose locus is to be determined is $P ( h, k )$ and it touches $y$-axis in the first quadrant and we know that if a circle touches the $y$-axis, then its radius is equal to the absolute value of the $x$-coordinate of the centre.

Hence, the radius of the circle is $= h .

Also, we know that if two circles touches externally, then the distance between their centres is equal to the sum of their radii.

And, the centre and radius of a circle ${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} = {r}^{2}$is \left(0, 0\right)$ and $1 respectively.

Now, since the circle with centre \left(h, k\right) and radius$h$ touches ${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} = 1$externally, then

$⇒ h + 1 = \sqrt{{h}^{2} + {k}^{2}}$

Squaring both the sides, we get

$⇒ {h}^{2} + 2h + 1 = {h}^{2} + {k}^{2}$

$⇒ {k}^{2} = 2h + 1

Now, to $get the locus, replace \left(h, k\right) by \left(x, y\right),$ to get

${y}^{2} = 2x + 1 .

Hence, the required locus is ${y}^{2} = 2x + 1$

$⇒ y = \sqrt{1 + 2x}, x \ge 0 .

Let $\omega$ be a complex number such that $2\omega + 1 = z$ where $z = \sqrt{- 3}$ . If

33923.sol:
$\omega = - \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}i$ (cube root of unity)

So, $1 + \omega + {\omega}^{2} = 0$ and ${\omega}^{3} =1$

Now $\left|\begin{cases}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & \omega & {\omega}^{2} \\ 1 & {\omega}^{2} & \omega\end{cases}\right| = 3\left({\omega}^{2} - \omega\right)$

So $k = {\omega}^{2} - \omega$

$⇒ k = \left(- \dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}i\right) - \left(- \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}i\right)$

$⇒ k = - \sqrt{3}i$

$⇒ k = - z$

34124.subject: Mathematics
34124.text: The value of the integral $\int_{-\pi/4}^{\pi/4}\left(\dfrac{32\cos^4 x}{1 + e^{\sin x}}\right)dx$ is:
34124.sol:
Let $I = \int_{-\pi/4}^{\pi/4} \dfrac{32\cos^4 x}{1 + e^{\sin x}} dx$

Using the definite integral property $\int_{-a}^{a} f(x) dx = \int_{0}^{a} (f(x) + f(-x)) dx$, we get:

$I = \int_{0}^{\pi/4} \left( \dfrac{32\cos^4 x}{1 + e^{\sin x}} + \dfrac{32\cos^4(-x)}{1 + e^{\sin(-x)}} \right) dx$

$I = \int_{0}^{\pi/4} \left( \dfrac{32\cos^4 x}{1 + e^{\sin x}} + \dfrac{32\cos^4 x}{1 + e^{-\sin x}} \right) dx$

$I = \int_{0}^{\pi/4} \left( \dfrac{32\cos^4 x}{1 + e^{\sin x}} + \dfrac{32\cos^4 x \cdot e^{\sin x}}{e^{\sin x} + 1} \right) dx$

$I = \int_{0}^{\pi/4} 32\cos^4 x \left( \dfrac{1 + e^{\sin x}}{1 + e^{\sin x}} \right) dx$

$I = \int_{0}^{\pi/4} 32\cos^4 x dx$

Using the trigonometric identity $\cos^2 x = \dfrac{1 + \cos 2x}{2}$, we can write:

$\cos^4 x = \left( \dfrac{1 + \cos 2x}{2} \right)^2 = \dfrac{1}{4} (1 + 2\cos 2x + \cos^2 2x)$

$\cos^4 x = \dfrac{1}{4} \left( 1 + 2\cos 2x + \dfrac{1 + \cos 4x}{2} \right) = \dfrac{3}{8} + \dfrac{1}{2}\cos 2x + \dfrac{1}{8}\cos 4x$

Substituting this back into the integral:

$I = 32 \int_{0}^{\pi/4} \left( \dfrac{3}{8} + \dfrac{1}{2}\cos 2x + \dfrac{1}{8}\cos 4x \right) dx$

$I = \int_{0}^{\pi/4} (12 + 16\cos 2x + 4\cos 4x) dx$

Integrating term by term:

$I = \left[ 12x + 8\sin 2x + \sin 4x \right]_{0}^{\pi/4}$

$I = \left( 12\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) + 8\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) + \sin(\pi) \right) - (0 + 0 + 0)$

$I = 3\pi + 8(1) + 0 = 3\pi + 8$

Answer: $3\pi + 8$

34611.text:
If the system of linear equations :

$\begin{aligned}
& x_1+2 x_2+3 x_3=6 \\
& x_1+3 x_2+5 x_3=9 \\
& 2 x_1+5 x_2+a x_3=b
\end{aligned}$

is consistent and has infinite number of solutions, then :
options:
$a=8, b$ can be any real number

$b=15, a$ can be any real number

$a \in R-\{8\}$ and $b \in R-\{15\}$

$a=8, b=15$
34611.sol:
Given system of equations can be written in matrix form as $\mathrm{AX}=\mathrm{B}$ where $\mathrm{A}=\left(\begin{array}{lll}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 3 & 5 \\ 2 & 5 & a\end{array}\right)$ and $\mathrm{B}=\left(\begin{array}{l}6 \\ 9 \\ b\end{array}\right)$

34791.text: Let $y = y\left(x\right)$ be the solution of the differential equation $xtan\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)dy = \left(ytan\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right) - x\right)dx$, $- 1 \le x \le 1, y\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{6} .$ Then the area of the region bounded by the curves $x = 0, x = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ and $y = y\left(x\right)$ in the upper half plane is:
34791.sol:
We have,

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{x\left(\dfrac{y}{x} \cdot tan\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right) - 1\right)}{xtan\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)}$
$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{y}{x} - cot\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)$

Put $y = vx$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = v + x\left(\dfrac{dv}{dx}\right)$

Now, we get

$v + x\left(\dfrac{dv}{dx}\right) = v - cotv$

$⇒ ∫ tanvdv = - ∫ \dfrac{dx}{x}$

$⇒ ln\left|secv\right| = - ln\left|x\right| + c$

$⇒ ln\left|sec\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)\right| = - ln\left|x\right| + c$

$⇒ ln\left|sec\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)\right| + ln\left|x\right| = c$

Now, $y\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$, then

$ln\left|sec\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)\right| + ln\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = c$

$⇒ ln2 + ln\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = c$

$⇒ ln2 - ln2 = c$

$⇒ c = 0$

Hence,

$∴ sec\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right) = \dfrac{1}{x}$

$⇒ cos\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right) = x$

$⇒ y = x\cos^{- 1}\left(x\right)$

So, required bounded area

$= {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}}\left(\mathop{\mathop{\cos^{- 1}x}_{⏟}}_{I}\right)\mathop{x}_{II}dx$

$= {\left[\cos^{- 1}x \cdot \left(\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2}\right)\right]}_{0}^{\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}} + \dfrac{1}{2}{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}}\left(\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{\sqrt{1 - {x}^{2}}}\right)dx$

$= \dfrac{\pi}{16} - \dfrac{1}{2}{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}}\left(\dfrac{1 - {x}^{2} - 1}{\sqrt{1 - {x}^{2}}}\right)dx$

$= \dfrac{\pi}{16} - \dfrac{1}{2}{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}}\left(\sqrt{1 - {x}^{2}} - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 - {x}^{2}}}\right)dx$

$= \dfrac{\pi}{16} - \dfrac{1}{2}{\left[\dfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{1 - {x}^{2}} + \dfrac{1}{2}\sin^{- 1}x - \sin^{- 1}x\right]}_{0}^{\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}}$

$= \dfrac{\pi}{16} - \dfrac{1}{2}{\left[\dfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{1 - {x}^{2}} - \dfrac{1}{2}\sin^{- 1}x\right]}_{0}^{\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}}$

$= \dfrac{\pi}{16} - \dfrac{1}{2}\left[\dfrac{1}{4} - \dfrac{\pi}{8}\right]$

$= \left(\dfrac{\pi - 1}{8}\right)$ sq. units

36459.text: The total number of $4$-digit numbers whose greatest common divisor with $18$ is $3$ is _____.
36459.sol:
Let $N$ be the four digit number $gcd\left(N, 18\right) = 3$

Hence $N$ is an odd integer which is divisible by $3$ but not by $9$.

$4$ digit odd multiples of $3$

$1005, 1011, \ldots , 9999 \to 1500$

digit odd multiples of $9$

$1017, 1035, \ldots , 9999 \to 500$

Hence number of such $N = 1500 - 500 = 1000$

&\Rightarrow $\frac{n !}{2 !(n-2) !} \cdot \frac{p^2(1-p)^n}{(1-p)^2}$\\

&\Rightarrow n p=3-p \\

36891.text: Let $a, b$ be two non-zero real numbers. If $p$ and $r$ are the roots of the equation ${x}^{2} - 8ax + 2a = 0$ and $q$ and $s$ are the roots of the equation ${x}^{2} + 12bx + 6b = 0$, such that $\dfrac{1}{p}, \dfrac{1}{q}, \dfrac{1}{r}, \dfrac{1}{s}$ are in A.P., then ${a}^{- 1} - {b}^{- 1}$ is equal to _____ .
36891.sol:
Since $p, r$ are roots of ${x}^{2} - 8ax + 2a = 0$ and

$q, s$ are the roots of ${x}^{2} + 12bx + 6b = 0$

So the equation $2a{x}^{2} - 8ax + 1 = 0$ has roots $\dfrac{1}{p}, \dfrac{1}{r}$ and

$6b{x}^{2} + 12bx + 1 = 0$ has roots $\dfrac{1}{q}, \dfrac{1}{s}$.

Given that $\dfrac{1}{p}, \dfrac{1}{q}, \dfrac{1}{r}, \dfrac{1}{s}$ are in A.P.

Let $\dfrac{1}{p} = \alpha - 3\beta, \dfrac{1}{q} = \alpha - \beta, \dfrac{1}{r} = \alpha + \beta$ and $\dfrac{1}{s} = \alpha + 3\beta$

i.e. $\dfrac{1}{p} + \dfrac{1}{r} = 2\alpha - 2\beta = 4$ and

$\dfrac{1}{q} + \dfrac{1}{s} = 2\alpha + 2\beta = - 2$

or $\alpha = \dfrac{1}{2}, \beta = - \dfrac{3}{2}$

i.e. $\dfrac{1}{p} = 5, \dfrac{1}{q} = 2, \dfrac{1}{r} = - 1, \dfrac{1}{s} = - 4$

Now

$\dfrac{1}{p} \times \dfrac{1}{r} = \dfrac{1}{2a} = - 5 ⇒ \dfrac{1}{a} = - 10$ and $\dfrac{1}{q} \times \dfrac{1}{s} = \dfrac{1}{6b} = - 8 ⇒ \dfrac{1}{b} = - 48$

Hence, ${a}^{- 1} - {b}^{- 1} = - 10 + 48 = 38$

The dielectric constant of the medium is $\_\_\_\_$ (speed of light in free space is $3 \times 10^{8} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$)
40283.sol:
From the wave equation $E_y = 20\sin(3 \times 10^6 x - 4.5 \times 10^{14} t)$:
Wave number: $k = 3 \times 10^6$ m⁻¹
Angular frequency: $\omega = 4.5 \times 10^{14}$ rad/s
Speed of wave in medium: $v = \frac{\omega}{k} = \frac{4.5 \times 10^{14}}{3 \times 10^6} = 1.5 \times 10^8$ m/s
Speed of light in vacuum: $c = 3 \times 10^8$ m/s
Refractive index: $n = \frac{c}{v} = \frac{3 \times 10^8}{1.5 \times 10^8} = 2$
For a nonmagnetic medium: $n = \sqrt{\epsilon_r}$
Dielectric constant: $\epsilon_r = n^2 = 4$

40393.text: The electric field of a plane polarized electromagnetic wave in free space at time $t = 0$ is given by the expression $\overset{\to}{E}\left(x, y\right) = 10\overset{^}{j}cos\left(6x + 8z\right)$. The magnetic field $\overset{\to}{B}\left(x, z, t\right)$ is given by ($c$ is the velocity of light.)
40393.sol:
$E = {E}_{0}cos\left(\omegat - \overset{\to}{K} \cdot \overset{\to}{r}\right)$

$∴$ At any time $t$,

$\overset{\to}{K} = 6\overset{^}{i} + 8\overset{^}{k}$

${B}_{0} = \dfrac{{E}_{0}}{c} = \dfrac{10}{c}$

$\lambda = \dfrac{2\pi}{k} = \dfrac{2\pi}{10} = \dfrac{\pi}{5}$

Also, $\overset{\to}{E} \times \overset{\to}{B} = \overset{\to}{c}$

$∴ \omega = 2\pif = \dfrac{2\pic}{\lambda}$

$\left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ {B}_{x} & {B}_{y} & {B}_{z}\end{cases}\right| = \dfrac{6\overset{^}{i} + 8\overset{^}{k}}{10}$

$\omega = \dfrac{2\pi \times c}{\left(\dfrac{\pi}{5}\right)} = 10c$

$∴ \overset{^}{i}\left[{B}_{z} - 0\right] + \overset{^}{j}\left(0\right) + \overset{^}{k}\left(- {B}_{x}\right) = 0.6\overset{^}{i} - 0.8\overset{^}{k}$

Comparing the coefficients on both sides,

$∴ {B}_{z} = 0.6; {B}_{x} = - 0.8$

$\left|\overset{\to}{{B}_{0}}\right| = \dfrac{10}{c}\left(- 0.8\overset{^}{i} + 0.6\overset{^}{k}\right) = \dfrac{- 8\overset{^}{i} + 6\overset{^}{k}}{c}$

So the magnetic field,$\overset{\to}{B} = \dfrac{1}{c}\left(- 8\overset{^}{i} + 6\overset{^}{k}\right)cos ⁡ \left(6x + 8z - 10ct\right)tesla$

40438.subject: Physics
40438.text:
Two metal plates $(A, B)$ are kept horizontally with separation of $\left(\dfrac{12}{\pi}\right)$ cm, with plate A on the top. An atomizer jet sprays oil (density $1.5$ g/cm$^3$) droplets of radius $1$ mm horizontally. All oil droplets carry a charge $5$ nC. The potentials $V_A and V_B$ are required on plates A and B respectively in order to ensure the droplets do not descend. The values of $V_A and V_B$ are _______.
(Neglect the air resistance to the droplets and take $g = 10$ m/s$^2$)
40438.sol:
For the oil droplets to not descend, the upward electric force must balance the downward gravitational force.

$qE = mg$

The mass of the oil droplet is given by:

$m = \dfrac{4}{3} \pi r^3 \rho$

Substituting the given values $r = 10^{-3}$ m and $\rho = 1500$ kg/m$^3$:

$m = \dfrac{4}{3} \pi (10^{-3})^3 \times 1500 = 2 \pi \times 10^{-6}$ kg

The electric field $E$ required is:

$E = \dfrac{mg}{q} = \dfrac{2 \pi \times 10^{-6} \times 10}{5 \times 10^{-9}} = 4000 \pi$ V/m

The potential difference $\Delta V$ between the plates is:

$\Delta V = E \times d = 4000 \pi \times \left(\dfrac{12}{\pi} \times 10^{-2}\right) = 480$ V

Since the charge on the droplet is positive, the electric field must be directed upwards to provide an upward force. Electric field lines point from higher potential to lower potential, so the bottom plate B must be at a higher potential than the top plate A.

$V_B - V_A = 480$ V

Checking the given options, $V_A = 100$ V and $V_B = 580$ V satisfies this condition.

Answer: $100 \, V$ and $580 \, V$

42187.subject: Physics
42187.text: The velocity ($v$) versus time ($t$) plot of a particle is shown in the figure, for a time interval of $40\text{ s}$. The total distance travelled by the particle and the average velocity during this period are, respectively _______.
42187.sol:
The total distance travelled by the particle is equal to the sum of the magnitudes of the areas under the velocity-time graph.

Area of the first triangle (from $t = 0$ to $t = 20\text{ s}$) is:
$A_1 = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 20 \times 5 = 50\text{ m}$

Magnitude of the area of the second triangle (from $t = 20$ to $t = 40\text{ s}$) is:
$|A_2| = \left| \dfrac{1}{2} \times 20 \times (-5) \right| = 50\text{ m}$

Total distance $= A_1 + |A_2| = 50 + 50 = 100\text{ m}$

The total displacement is the algebraic sum of the areas under the velocity-time graph.

Total displacement $= A_1 + A_2 = 50 - 50 = 0\text{ m}$

Average velocity is the ratio of total displacement to total time.

Average velocity $= \dfrac{\text{Total displacement}}{\text{Total time}} = \dfrac{0}{40} = 0$

Answer: $100\text{ m}$ and zero

42494.subject: Physics
42494.text: Two nuclei of mass number $3$ combine with another nucleus of mass number $4$ to yield a nucleus of mass number $10$. If the binding energy per nucleon for the mass numbers $3$, $4$ and $10$ are $5.6$ MeV, $7.4$ MeV and $6.1$ MeV, respectively, then in the process, $\Delta Mc^2 = $ _____ MeV.
42494.sol:
The nuclear reaction is given by:

$2 X^{3} + Y^{4} \rightarrow Z^{10}$

The total binding energy of the reactants is the sum of the binding energies of the two nuclei of mass number $3$ and the nucleus of mass number $4$.

Binding energy of reactants $= 2 \times (3 \times 5.6) + (4 \times 7.4)$

$= 33.6 + 29.6 = 63.2$ MeV

The total binding energy of the product nucleus of mass number $10$ is:

Binding energy of product $= 10 \times 6.1 = 61.0$ MeV

The change in mass energy $\Delta M c^2$ is equal to the difference in the total binding energies of the reactants and the product.

$\Delta M c^2 = |63.2 - 61.0| = 2.2$ MeV

Answer: $2.2$

44192.subject: Physics
44192.text: In Young's double slit experiment, the fringe width of the interference pattern produced on the screen is $2.4$ $\mu$m. If the experiment is carried out in another medium having refractive index $1.2$, the fringe width will be _____ $\mu$m.
44192.sol:
The fringe width in Young's double slit experiment is given by $\beta = \dfrac{\lambda D}{d}$.

When the experiment is performed in a medium of refractive index $\mu$, the wavelength of light becomes $\lambda' = \dfrac{\lambda}{\mu}$.

The new fringe width is $\beta' = \dfrac{\lambda' D}{d} = \dfrac{\lambda D}{\mu d} = \dfrac{\beta}{\mu}$.

Substituting the given values, $\beta = 2.4$ $\mu$m and $\mu = 1.2$:

$\beta' = \dfrac{2.4}{1.2} = 2$ $\mu$m.

Answer: $2$

48542.text: The equation of the normal to the curve \( $y\left($1+x^{2}\right)=2-x \) where the tangent crosses \( x \)-axis is
48542.sol:
Given curve, $y\left(1+x^{2}\right)=2-x \rightarrow(1)$
At x-axis, $y=0$ so Eq. (1) becomes
$\Rightarrow 0=2-x \Rightarrow x=2$
So, the point is $(2,0)$
Now, differentiate Eq. (1) with respect to x, we get
$y^{\prime}\left(1+x^{2}\right)+y(2 x)=-1$
At point $(2,0)$, we have
$\Rightarrow y^{\prime}\left(1+2^{2}\right)+0(2 \times 2)=-1\Rightarrow y^{\prime}(5)=-1 \Rightarrow y^{\prime}=\frac{-1}{5}$
This is the slope of the tangent at point $(2,0)$
So, slope of normal is
$-\frac{1}{y^{\prime}}=5$
Therefore, equation of normal is,
$y-0=5(x-2)\Rightarrow y=5 x-10\Rightarrow 5 x-y-10=0$

49264.subject: Mathematics
49264.text: If A and B are invertible matrices of same order, then which of the following is not correct?
49264.sol:
For any square matrix $A$ of order $n$, the fundamental property relating the matrix and its adjoint is $A \cdot (\text{adj}A) = (\text{adj}A) \cdot A = |A| I$, where $I$ is the identity matrix of order $n$.

Thus, the statement $A \cdot (\text{adj}A) = (\text{adj}A) \cdot A = A I$ is incorrect.

Since $A$ and $B$ are invertible matrices, their determinants must be non-zero, which means $|A| \neq 0$ and $|B| \neq 0$.

The reversal law for the inverse of the product of two invertible matrices states that $(AB)^{-1} = B^{-1} A^{-1}$.

Therefore, the only incorrect statement is the first one.

Answer: $A \cdot (\text{adj}A) = (\text{adj}A) \cdot A = A I$

55118.subject: Chemistry
55118.text: Identify the product 'Y' in the following reaction $\text{Benzonitrile} \xrightarrow{\large{\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{MgBr} / \text{dry ether}}} X \xrightarrow{\large{\text{H}_3\text{O}^+}} Y + \text{MgBr(OH)} + \text{NH}_3$
55118.sol:
Benzonitrile is $C_6H_5CN$.

When benzonitrile reacts with phenylmagnesium bromide ($C_6H_5MgBr$) in the presence of dry ether, a nucleophilic addition takes place at the electrophilic carbon of the cyanide group, forming an imine salt intermediate ($X$).

$C_6H_5CN + C_6H_5MgBr \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} (C_6H_5)_2C=NMgBr$

Upon acid hydrolysis ($H_3O^+$), the imine salt intermediate ($X$) is converted into a ketone.

$(C_6H_5)_2C=NMgBr \xrightarrow{H_3O^+} (C_6H_5)_2C=O + NH_3 + MgBr(OH)$

The product $Y$ is $(C_6H_5)_2C=O$, which is benzophenone.

Answer: Benzophenone

59411.text: A gaseous mixture of $\mathrm{O}_2$ and $\mathrm{CH}_4$ are in the ratio $1: 4$ by mass. Find the ratio of their molecules.
59411.sol:
Ratio of molecules is proportional to the ratio of moles. Given mass ratio $m_{\mathrm{O}_2} : m_{\mathrm{CH}_4} = 1 : 4$, let $m_{\mathrm{O}_2} = x$ and $m_{\mathrm{CH}_4} = 4x$.

Using molar masses $M_{\mathrm{O}_2} = 32$ g/mol and $M_{\mathrm{CH}_4} = 16$ g/mol, the moles are:

$n_{\mathrm{O}_2} = \frac{x}{32}$,
$n_{\mathrm{CH}_4} = \frac{4x}{16} = \frac{x}{4}$.

The ratio $n_{\mathrm{O}_2} : n_{\mathrm{CH}_4} = \frac{x}{32} : \frac{x}{4} = 1 : 8$.

Thus, the molecular ratio is $\boxed{1:8}$.

61060.sol:
The integral $I = \int_0^1 \log \left(\frac{1}{x} - 1\right) \, \mathrm{d}x$ is evaluated by simplifying the logarithmic argument to $\log \left(\frac{1-x}{x}\right)$.
Applying the substitution property $\int_a^b f(x) \, \mathrm{d}x = \int_a^b f(a+b-x) \, \mathrm{d}x$ with $a=0$, $b=1$ yields $I = \int_0^1 \log \left(\frac{x}{1-x}\right) \, \mathrm{d}x$.

Adding both forms of $I$ gives $2I = \int_0^1 \left[ \log \left(\frac{1-x}{x}\right) + \log \left(\frac{x}{1-x}\right) \right] \, \mathrm{d}x = \int_0^1 \log(1) \, \mathrm{d}x$.

Since $\log(1) = 0$, it follows that $2I = 0$, and thus $I = 0$.

Final answer: $\boxed{0}$

61264.text: If the solution of the differential equation $(1 + x^3)\dfrac{dy}{dx} + 6x^2y = 1 + x^2$ is $y = \dfrac{1}{(1 + x^3)^s}   \left[x + \dfrac{x^p}{p} + \dfrac{x^q}{q} + \dfrac{x^r}{r} +$ c\right]$, then the LCM of $p, q, r$ and $s$ is...$
61264.sol:
The given differential equation is $(1 + x^3)\dfrac{dy}{dx} + 6x^2y = 1 + x^2$.

Dividing by $(1 + x^3)$, we get a linear differential equation of the form $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + P(x)y = Q(x)$:

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{6x^2}{1 + x^3}y = \dfrac{1 + x^2}{1 + x^3}$

The integrating factor (IF) is given by:

$\text{IF} = e^{\int P(x) dx} = e^{\int \dfrac{6x^2}{1 + x^3} dx}$

Let $1 + x^3 = t$, then $3x^2 dx = dt$, which gives $6x^2 dx = 2 dt$.

$\int \dfrac{6x^2}{1 + x^3} dx = \int \dfrac{2}{t} dt = 2 \ln t = \ln(t^2) = \ln((1 + x^3)^2)$

Thus, $\text{IF} = e^{\ln((1 + x^3)^2)} = (1 + x^3)^2$.

Multiplying the differential equation by the IF, we get:

$\dfrac{d}{dx} \left[ y (1 + x^3)^2 \right] = \dfrac{1 + x^2}{1 + x^3} \times (1 + x^3)^2$

$\dfrac{d}{dx} \left[ y (1 + x^3)^2 \right] = (1 + x^2)(1 + x^3)$

$\dfrac{d}{dx} \left[ y (1 + x^3)^2 \right] = 1 + x^2 + x^3 + x^5$

Integrating both sides with respect to $x$:

$y (1 + x^3)^2 = \int (1 + x^2 + x^3 + x^5) dx$

$y (1 + x^3)^2 = x + \dfrac{x^3}{3} + \dfrac{x^4}{4} + \dfrac{x^6}{6} + c$

$y = \dfrac{1}{(1 + x^3)^2} \left[x + \dfrac{x^3}{3} + \dfrac{x^4}{4} + \dfrac{x^6}{6} +$ c \right]$

Comparing this with the given solution $y = $\dfrac{1}{(1 + x^3)^s}\left[x + \dfrac{x^p}{p} + \dfrac{x^q}{q} + \dfrac{x^r}{r} + c\right]$, we find:

$s = 2$

The set of values for $\{p, q, r\}$ is $\{3, 4, 6\}$.

We need to find the LCM of $p, q, r$ and $s$, which is the LCM of $3, 4, 6,$ and $2$.

$\text{LCM}(2, 3, 4, 6) = 12$

Answer: $12$

61702.text: If $x=a \sin 2 t(1+\cos 2 t), y=b \cos 2 t(1-\cos 2 t)$ then $\frac{d y}{d x}$ is equal to
61702.sol:
The derivative $\frac{dy}{dx}$ is found using parametric differentiation: $\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{dy/dt}{dx/dt}$.
Given $x = a \sin 2t (1 + \cos 2t)$ and $y = b \cos 2t (1 - \cos 2t)$, we compute the derivatives.

Differentiating $x$ using the product rule:

$\frac{dx}{dt} = a[(2 \cos 2t)(1 + \cos 2t) + \sin 2t(-2 \sin 2t)] = 2a[\cos 2t + (\cos^2 2t - \sin^2 2t)]$

Applying the double angle identity $\cos 4t = \cos^2 2t - \sin^2 2t$:

$\frac{dx}{dt} = 2a(\cos 2t + \cos 4t)$

Using the sum-to-product identity: $\cos 2t + \cos 4t = 2 \cos 3t \cos(-t) = 2 \cos 3t \cos t$

Thus, $\frac{dx}{dt} = 4a \cos 3t \cos t$

Differentiating $y$ similarly:

$\frac{dy}{dt} = b[(-2 \sin 2t)(1 - \cos 2t) + \cos 2t(2 \sin 2t)] = 2b[-\sin 2t + 2 \sin 2t \cos 2t]$

Using $2 \sin 2t \cos 2t = \sin 4t$:

$\frac{dy}{dt} = 2b(\sin 4t - \sin 2t)$

Applying the identity: $\sin 4t - \sin 2t = 2 \cos 3t \sin t$

Thus, $\frac{dy}{dt} = 4b \cos 3t \sin t$

Now $\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{4b \cos 3t \sin t}{4a \cos 3t \cos t} = \frac{b}{a} \tan t$ for $\cos 3t eq 0$

This corresponds to option A.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{A}}$

62010.subject: Mathematics
62010.text: The domain of the function $f(x) = e^{\sqrt{5x - 3 - 2x^2}}$ is
62010.sol:
For the function $f(x) = e^{\sqrt{5x - 3 - 2x^2}}$ to be defined, the expression inside the square root must be non-negative.

$5x - 3 - 2x^2 \ge 0$

$2x^2 - 5x + 3 \le 0$

$2x^2 - 2x - 3x + 3 \le 0$

$2x(x - 1) - 3(x - 1) \le 0$

$(2x - 3)(x - 1) \le 0$

$1 \le x \le \dfrac{3}{2}$

The domain of the function is $\left[1, \dfrac{3}{2}\right]$.

Answer: $\left[1, \dfrac{3}{2}\right]$

62022.subject: Mathematics
62022.text: Which of the following is not a homogeneous function?
62022.sol:
A function $f(x, y)$ is homogeneous of degree $n$ if $f(tx, ty) = t^n f(x, y)$ for all $t > 0$ and some real $n$.

Function A: $f(tx, ty) = (ty)^2 + 2(tx)(ty) = t^2(y^2 + 2xy) = t^2 f(x, y)$, homogeneous of degree 2.

Function B: $f(tx, ty) = 2(tx) - 3(ty) = t(2x - 3y) = t f(x, y)$, homogeneous of degree 1.

Function C: $f(tx, ty) = \sin\left(\frac{ty}{tx}\right) = \sin\left(\frac{y}{x}\right) = f(x, y)$, homogeneous of degree 0.

Function D: $f(tx, ty) = \cos(tx) + \sin(ty)$ cannot be expressed as $t^n(\cos x + \sin y)$ for any $n$. For example, with $t = 2$, $f(2x, 2y) = \cos(2x) + \sin(2y) \neq 2^n(\cos x + \sin y)$ for all $n \in \mathbb{R}$.

$\therefore$ The non-homogeneous function is $\boxed{D}$.

63946.text: In $\triangle ABC$, with usual notations, $(a + b + c)(b + c - a)(c + a - b)(a + b - c) = 3b^2c^2$, then $\angle A = $
63946.sol:
Given $(a + b + c)(b + c - a)(c + a - b)(a + b - c) = 3b^2c^2$

Grouping the terms:

$((b + c) + a)((b + c) - a)(a - (b - c))(a + (b - c)) = 3b^2c^2$

$((b + c)^2 - a^2)(a^2 - (b - c)^2) = 3b^2c^2$

$(b^2 + c^2 + 2bc - a^2)(a^2 - (b^2 + c^2 - 2bc)) = 3b^2c^2$

$(2bc + (b^2 + c^2 - a^2))(2bc - (b^2 + c^2 - a^2)) = 3b^2c^2$

Using the algebraic identity $(x+y)(x-y) = x^2 - y^2$:

$4b^2c^2 - (b^2 + c^2 - a^2)^2 = 3b^2c^2$

$(b^2 + c^2 - a^2)^2 = b^2c^2$

$b^2 + c^2 - a^2 = \pm bc$

Dividing by $2bc$:

$\dfrac{b^2 + c^2 - a^2}{2bc} = \pm \dfrac{1}{2}$

Using the cosine rule, $\cos A = \dfrac{b^2 + c^2 - a^2}{2bc}$:

$\cos A = \pm \dfrac{1}{2}$

Since $0^{}^{\circ} < A < 180^{}^{\circ}$, we get $A = 60^{}^{\circ}$ or $120^{}^{\circ}$.

Answer: $60^{}^{\circ}$ or $120^{}^{\circ}$

65575.subject: Physics
65575.text: In series LCR circuit C = 2 uF, L=1 mH and R= 10 $\Omega$. What is the ratio of energies stored in the capacitor and inductor when maximum current flows through circuit?
65575.sol:
For a series LCR circuit undergoing free oscillations, the voltage equation is given by:

$V_L + V_R + V_C = 0$

$L \dfrac{di}{dt} + iR + V_C = 0$

When the current $i$ in the circuit is maximum, its rate of change is zero, i.e., $\dfrac{di}{dt} = 0$.

Substituting this into the voltage equation, we get:

$0 + i_\maxR + V_C = 0 \Rightarrow V_C = -i_\maxR$

The energy stored in the capacitor at this instant is:

$U_C = \dfrac{1}{2} C V_C^2 = \dfrac{1}{2} C (i_\maxR)^2$

The energy stored in the inductor at the same instant is:

$U_L = \dfrac{1}{2} L i_\max^2$

The ratio of the energy stored in the capacitor to that in the inductor is:

$\dfrac{U_C}{U_L} = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2} C i_\max^2 R^2}{\dfrac{1}{2} L i_\max^2} = \dfrac{CR^2}{L}$

Given values are:

$C = 2 \times 10^{-6} \text{ F}$

$R = 10 \Omega$

$L = 10^{-3} \text{ H}$

Substituting the given values into the ratio:

$\dfrac{U_C}{U_L} = \dfrac{2 \times 10^{-6} \times (10)^2}{10^{-3}}$

$\dfrac{U_C}{U_L} = \dfrac{2 \times 10^{-4}}{10^{-3}} = 0.2$

Thus, the ratio of energies is $0.2 : 1$.

Answer: $0.2 : 1$

67001.text:
The point charges $+q$, $-q$, $-q$, $+q$, $+Q$ and $-q$ are placed at the vertices of a regular hexagon ABCDEF as shown in the figure.

The electric field at the centre of the hexagon 'O' due to the five charges at A, B, C, D and F is thrice the electric field at centre 'O' due to charge $+Q$ at E alone. The value of Q is
67001.sol:
Let the distance from each vertex of the regular hexagon to its center O be $r$.

The electric field at the center O due to a point charge $q$ at a distance $r$ has a magnitude $E = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0}\dfrac{q}{r^2}$.

In the regular hexagon ABCDEF, the pairs of diametrically opposite vertices are (A, D), (B, E), and (C, F).

The charges at A and D are both $+q$. The electric fields produced by these two charges at the center O are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction, thus they cancel each other out.

The charges at C and F are both $-q$. The electric fields produced by these two charges at O are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction (pointing towards C and F respectively), thus they also cancel each other out.

Therefore, the net electric field at the center O due to the five charges at A, B, C, D, and F is solely the electric field produced by the charge $-q$ at B.

The magnitude of this field is $E_1 = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0}\dfrac{q}{r^2}$.

The electric field at O due to the charge $+Q$ at E alone has a magnitude $E_2 = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0}\dfrac{Q}{r^2}$.

67669.text: A circular coil of N turns and diameter D carries current I. It is unwound and rewound to make another coil of diameter 2D, current I remaining the same. The ratio of magnetic moments of the original coil to the new coil is

For the original coil:

$M_1 = NI \left( \dfrac{\pi D^2}{4} \right)

For the new coil:

$ M_2 = N' I $\left( \dfrac{\pi (2D)^2}{4} \right) = \left( \dfrac{N}{2} \right) I (\piD^2) = 2 NI \left( \dfrac{\pi D^2}{4} \right)$

Taking the ratio of the magnetic moments:

$\dfrac{M_1}{M_2} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Answer: $1:2$

68175.subject: Physics
68175.text: The surface energy of a liquid drop is "V". It is sprayed into 1000 equal droplets. The surface energy of all the droplets is
68175.sol:
Let R be the initial radius and A = 4$\pi$ R^2 the initial surface area of the liquid drop. Given the surface energy V = T $\times4\pi$ R^2, where T is the surface tension.

The drop is sprayed into 1000 equal droplets, each with radius r. Since the volume remains constant:

$\frac{4}{3}\pi R^3 = 1000 \times \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3$

Simplifying gives $R^3 = 1000r^3$, thus $R = 10r$ and $r = R/10$.

The total surface area of the droplets becomes:

$A' = 1000 \times 4\pi r^2 = 1000 \times 4\pi (R/10)^2 = 1000 \times 4\pi R^2/100 = 10A$

The new surface energy is therefore:

$V' = T \times A' = T \times 10A = 10V$

The total surface energy becomes $10V$.

69974.subject: Physics
69974.text: When the heat is given to a gas in an Isothermal process, then there will be
options: external work done and also rise in temperature.
69974.sol:
In an isothermal process, temperature remains constant (\Delta T = 0$). For an ideal gas, internal energy depends solely on temperature, so \Delta U = 0$.

The First Law of Thermodynamics gives $\Delta Q = \Delta U + \Delta W$. Substituting $\Delta U = 0$ yields $\Delta Q = \Delta W$.

Since heat is supplied (\Delta Q > 0$), the gas does positive work on its surroundings (\Delta W > 0$).

Option analysis:
A) External work done: consistent with derivation
B) Rise in temperature: contradicts isothermal condition
C) Increase in internal energy: contradicts $\Delta U = 0$
D) External work and temperature rise: partially incorrect

The supplied heat is converted entirely into external work done by the gas.

70591.text:
A wire PQ has length $4.8 \mathrm{ m}$ and mass $0.06 \mathrm{ kg}$. Another wire QR has length $2.56 \mathrm{ m}$ and mass $0.2 \mathrm{ kg}$. Both wires have same radii and are joined as a single wire. This wire is under tension of $80 \mathrm{ N}$. A wave pulse of amplitude $3.5 \mathrm{ cm}$ is sent along the wire $\mathrm{PQ}$ from end $\mathrm{P}$.
The time taken by the wave to reach the other end of single wire is (No power is dissipated during propagation)
70591.sol:
Mass per unit length for wire $P Q$,
$\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{PQ}}=\frac{\mathrm{M}}{\mathrm{L}}=\frac{0.06}{4.8}=\frac{1}{80} \mathrm{ kg} / \mathrm{m}$
Similarly for wire $\mathrm{QR}$,
$\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{QR}}=\frac{0.2}{2.56}=\frac{5}{64} \mathrm{ kg} / \mathrm{m}\therefore \quad$ Velocity of the wave in PQ wire:
$y=\sqrt{\frac{T}{m_{\mathrm{PQ}}}}=\sqrt{\frac{80}{1 / 80}}=80 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s}\therefore \quad$ Time taken to travel PQ wire, $\mathrm{t}=\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{v}}=\frac{4.8}{80}=0.06 \mathrm{ s}$ Velocity of wave in QR wire,
$\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{v} & =\sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{T}_{\text{net }}^{\prime}}{\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{QR}}}}=\sqrt{\frac{(80+0.6) \times 64}{5}} \\
& =32.12 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s}
\end{aligned}\therefore \quad$ Time taken to travel $\mathrm{QR}$ wire, $\mathrm{t}=\frac{2.56}{32.12}=0.08 \mathrm{ s}$
So, total time taken will be:
$\mathrm{t}=0.06+0.08=0.14 \mathrm{ s}$

71778.subject: Chemistry
71778.text: How is the molar conductivity of an elecrolytic solution calculated?
options: electrolytic conductivity multiplied by molar concentration
molar concentration / square of electrolytic conductivity x 1000
71778.sol:
Molar conductivity (\Lambda_m$) is defined as the conducting power of all the ions produced by dissolving one mole of an electrolyte in a solution.

Mathematically, it is expressed as:

\Lambda_m = \dfrac{\kappa \times 1000}{C}$

where $\kappa$ is the electrolytic conductivity (specific conductance) in $S \, cm^{-1}$ and $C$ is the molar concentration of the solution in $mol \, L^{-1}$.

Thus, molar conductivity is calculated as electrolytic conductivity $\times 1000$ / molar concentration.

Answer: electrolytic conductivity x 1000 / molar concentration

72483.subject: Physics
72483.text: Two identical straight wires are stretched so as to produce 8 beats per second when vibrating simultaneously with tensions $T_1$ and $T_2$ respectively. On changing the tensions, the beat frequency remains unchanged. This will happen when $(T_1 > T_2)$
options: both $T_1$ and $T_2$ is decreased by value 256 N
both $T_1$ and $T_2$ is increased by value 256 N
72483.sol:
The frequency of a stretched wire is given by $f = \dfrac{1}{2L} \sqrt{\dfrac{T}{\mu}}$.

Since $T_1 > T_2$, the initial frequencies satisfy $f_1 > f_2$.

The initial beat frequency is $f_1 - f_2 = 8$.

For the beat frequency to remain unchanged after changing the tensions, the new frequencies must satisfy $|f_1' - f_2'| = 8$.

If $T_1$ is changed while $T_2$ is kept constant, we need $|f_1' - f_2| = 8$. Since $f_1 - f_2 = 8$, the only other possibility is $f_2 - f_1' = 8 \Rightarrow f_1' = f_2 - 8 = f_1 - 16$. This requires $f_1$ to decrease, meaning $T_1$ must be decreased.

If $T_2$ is changed while $T_1$ is kept constant, we need $|f_1 - f_2'| = 8$. Since $f_1 - f_2 = 8$, the only other possibility is $f_2' - f_1 = 8 \Rightarrow f_2' = f_1 + 8 = f_2 + 16$. This requires $f_2$ to increase, meaning $T_2$ must be increased.

Thus, the beat frequency can remain unchanged if $T_1$ is decreased or $T_2$ is increased.

Answer: $T_1$ is decreased or $T_2$ is increased

73823.text: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct?
options: A scale measuring hydrogen ion concentration in a solution is called pH scale
The higher the hydrogen ion concentration in a solution, higher is its pH
We can measure pH generally from 0 to 14 on a pH scale
The 'p' in pH stands for 'potenz' in German meaning power
73823.sol:
The pH of a solution is defined as the negative logarithm to the base $10$ of the hydrogen ion concentration, expressed as $pH = -\log_{10}[H^+]$.

Because of the negative sign in the formula, an increase in the hydrogen ion concentration $[H^+]$ results in a decrease in the pH value. Therefore, the higher the hydrogen ion concentration in a solution, the lower is its pH.

The other statements are correct: the pH scale measures hydrogen ion concentration, it generally ranges from $0$ to $14$, and the 'p' stands for 'potenz' (meaning power) in German.

Answer: The higher the hydrogen ion concentration in a solution, higher is its pH

77866.subject: Mathematics
77866.text:
Passage: A 4-digit number is selected at random formed by using the digits $0$, $1$, $2$, $3$ and $4$ (where repetition of digits is not allowed).

Question: What is the probability that the number selected does not contain zero at any position ?
77866.sol:
The total number of $4$-digit numbers formed using the digits $0, 1, 2, 3, 4$ without repetition is calculated by filling the thousands place in $4$ ways (excluding $0$) and the remaining $3$ places in ^{4}P_{3}$ ways.

Total outcomes = 4 \times 4 \times 3 \times 2 = 96$

The number of $4$-digit numbers formed without using $0$ at any position means using only the digits $1, 2, 3, 4$.

Favorable outcomes = ^{4}P_{4} = 4 \times 3 \times 2 \times 1 = 24$

Required probability = \dfrac{24}{96} = \dfrac{1}{4} = 0.25$

Answer: $0\cdot25$

77976.subject: Mathematics
77976.text: For a Binomial distribution with mean $6$ and standard deviation $\sqrt{2}, what is the value of $P(X=0)$ ?$
77976.sol:
Let $n$ be the number of trials and $p$ be the probability of success.

Mean $= np = 6$

Standard deviation $= \sqrt{npq} = \sqrt{2}$

Variance $= npq = 2$

Dividing the variance by the mean:

$\dfrac{npq}{np} = \dfrac{2}{6}$

$q = \dfrac{1}{3}$

Since $p + q = 1$, we get $p = \dfrac{2}{3}$.

Substituting $p$ into the mean equation:

$n\left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right) = 6 \Rightarrow n = 9$

The probability of $X = 0$ is given by:

$P(X=0) = ^{n}C_{0} p^0 q^n$

$P(X=0) = ^{9}C_{0} \left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right)^0 \left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)^9 = \left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)^9$

Answer: $\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)^9$

79525.sol:
Pearl is obtained from Pinctada vulgaris.
Related Theory
Pinctada (pearl oyster) belongs to phylum Mollusc. It is bilaterally symmetrical, triploblastic and coelomate animal. Body is covered by a calcareous shell and is unsegmented with a distinct head, muscular foot and visceral hump. A soft and spongy layer of skin forms a mantle over the visceral hump, the space between the hump and the mantle is called the mantle cavity in which feather like gills are present. The anterior head region has sensory tentacles and the mouth contains a file-like rasping organ for feeding, called radula. They are usually dioecious and oviparous with indirect development.

82235.subject: Physics
82235.text: The ratio of wavelengths of the last line of the Balmer series and the last line of the Lyman series is_____.
82235.sol:
For last Balmer series,
$\dfrac{1}{{\lambda}_{b}} = R\left[\dfrac{1}{{2}^{2}} - \dfrac{1}{{\infty}^{2}}\right]$
${\lambda}_{b} = \dfrac{4}{R}$
For last Lyman series,
$\dfrac{1}{{\lambda}_{l}} = R\left[\dfrac{1}{{1}^{2}} - \dfrac{1}{{\infty}^{2}}\right]$
${\lambda}_{l} = \dfrac{1}{R}$
$\dfrac{{\lambda}_{b}}{{\lambda}_{l}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{4}{R}}{\dfrac{1}{R}}$
$\dfrac{{\lambda}_{b}}{{\lambda}_{l}} = 4$

Hence this is the correct answer.

82265.text: A parallel plate air capacitor of capacitance $C$ is connected to a cell of emf $V$ and then disconnected from it. A dielectric slab of dielectric constant $K$, which can just fill the air gap of the capacitor, is now inserted in it. Which of the following is incorrect?

The energy stored in the capacitor decreases $K$ times.
The change in energy stored is $\dfrac{1}{2}C{V}^{2}\left(\dfrac{1}{K} - 1\right)$.
The charge on the capacitor is not conserved.

For air $K = 1$,
${C}_{1} = C$
$q = {C}_{1}V \ldots \left(i\right)$.
The charge remains constant.
${U}_{1} = \dfrac{{q}^{2}}{2C}$
${U}_{2} = \dfrac{{q}^{2}}{2CK}$
Change in energy stored in the capacitor,
$U = {U}_{2} - {U}_{1}$
$= \dfrac{{q}^{2}}{2C}\left(\dfrac{1}{K} - 1\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}C{V}^{2}\left(\dfrac{1}{K} - 1\right)$
$V ' = \dfrac{q}{CK} ⇒ V ' = \dfrac{V}{K}$
Here,1- Potential difference between the plates decreases by $K$ times.
2- The change in energy stored $∆ U = \dfrac{1}{2}C{V}^{2}\left(\dfrac{1}{K} - 1\right)$.
3- Charge is conserved.
4- The energy stored in capacitor decrease by $K, {U}_{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{{q}^{2}}{CK}$.

reflected light is partially polarized and the angle of reflection is close to $30^{\circ}$

transmitted light is completely polarized with angle of refraction close to $30^{\circ}$
83736.sol:

Using Brewster's Law
$\begin{aligned}
& \mu=\tan \left(i_p\right) \\
& 1.73=\tan \left(i_p\right) \\
& i_p=60^{\circ}
\end{aligned}$
By Law of reflection,
$i_p=r=60^{\circ}$

$N =$ Population density at time t$r =$ Intrinsic rate of natural increase

$K =$ Carrying capacity

When $\dfrac{N}{K} = 1$ then

$\dfrac{K - \text{​}N}{K} = 0$

Therefore,

$\dfrac{dN}{dt} = 0$

90560.subject: Mathematics
90560.text: The product of a $9 \times 4$ matrix and a $4 \times 9$ matrix contains a variable $x$ in exactly two places. If $D\left(x\right)$ is the determinant of the matrix product such that $D\left(0\right) = 1, D\left(- 1\right) = 1$ and $D\left(2\right) = 7$, then $D\left(- 2\right)$ is equal to
90560.sol:
Let, the order of matrix $A$ is $9 \times 4$ and matrix $B$ is $4 \times 9$
$D\left(x\right) = AB =$ a polynomial of degree $2$ as it has $x$ at $2$ places.
Let, $D\left(x\right) = a{x}^{2} + bx + c$
$D\left(0\right) = c = 1$
$D\left(- 1\right) = a - b + c = 1 ⇒ a - b = 0$
$D\left(2\right) = 4a + 2b + c = 7 ⇒ 4a + 2b = 6$
$⇒ 2a + b = 3$
Solving these two equations, we get,

$a = 1, b = 1$
$⇒ D\left(x\right) = {x}^{2} + x + 1$
$⇒ D\left(- 2\right) = 4 - 2 + 1 = 3$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{\left(\dfrac{cos^{2}\theta}{25} + \dfrac{sin^{2}\theta}{9}\right)} = 4$
$⇒ \dfrac{{cos}^{2}\theta}{25} + \dfrac{1 - {cos}^{2}\theta}{9} = \dfrac{1}{16}$
$⇒ cos ⁡ \theta = \dfrac{5\sqrt{7}}{16}$
If $l$ be the length of the tangent then $l^{2} = S^{'}$
or $l^{2} = 25cos^{2}\theta + 9sin^{2}\theta - 16 = 16cos^{2}\theta - 7$
$= 16 . \dfrac{25.7}{{\left(16\right)}^{2}} - 7 = \dfrac{175 - 112}{16} = \dfrac{63}{16}$
$⇒ l = \dfrac{3}{4}\sqrt{7}$& units

92520.subject: Physics
92520.text: Which among the following has a Hydrogen-like spectrum and whose lines have wavelengths four times shorter than those of atomic Hydrogen?
92520.sol:
For Hydrogen like atom, $\dfrac{1}{\lambda '}=R ⁡ Z{⁡}^{2} \left(1{n}_{1}^{2} - 1{n}_{2}^{2}\right) ...(i)

For Hydrogen atom, \dfrac{1}{λ}$=$ R ⁡ \left(1{n}_{1}^{2} - 1{n}_{2}^{2}\right) ...(ii)

Dividing Eqn (ii) by Eqn (i), we get

\dfrac{\lambda '}{λ} =\dfrac{R ⁡ \left(1{n}_{1}^{2} - 1{n}_{2}^{2}\right)}{{RZ}^{2}\left(1{n}_{1}^{2} - 1{n}_{2}^{2}\right)}$

$\text{or}\dfrac{\lambda '}{λ} =\dfrac{1}{Z{⁡}^{2}}$

According to problem, ${λ}^{'} = \dfrac{λ}{4}$

∴ $\dfrac{\lambda '}{4{λ}^{'}} = \dfrac{1}{Z{⁡}^{2}}$

$∴ Z = 2$

The atomic number of Helium atom is $2$. Hence, the required element is Helium.

From energy conservation,

Energy at lowest point = Energy at topmost point

$\dfrac{1}{2}{mv}^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}{mv}^{2} + \text{mg2}\text{l} \ldots \left(\text{ii}\text{i}\right)

$ v^{2} = u^{2} - 4$\text{g}\text{l} \ldots \left(\text{i}\text{v}\right)

From Eqns. (iv) and (v),

$⇒ F = \dfrac{2Tm}{d^{2} ⋅ ρ}$

$\text{T} = 2 \text{\pi} \sqrt{\dfrac{\text{I}}{\text{mgl}}}$

Here, $I$ = moment of inertia of the ring about the point of suspension

& $= mr^{2} + mr^{2}$

& $= 2mr^{2}$

and l = distance of the point of suspension from the centre of gravity& = r

$∴ \text{T} = 2 \text{\pi} \sqrt{\dfrac{2 {mr}^{2}}{\text{mgr}}} = 2 \text{\pi} \sqrt{\dfrac{\text{2r}}{\text{g}}}$

$∴ \text{Angular frequency} \text{\omega} = \dfrac{2 \text{\pi}}{\text{T}}$

$\text{or} \text{\omega} = \sqrt{\dfrac{\text{g}}{\text{2r}}}$

94113.text: An elastic string has a force constant $k$ and mass $m$. The string hangs vertically and a block of unknown mass is attached to its bottom end. It is known that the mass of the block is much greater than that of the string. The hanging block stretches the string the twice it's the relaxed length. How long $\left(t\right)$ would it take for a low amplitude transverse pulse to travel the length of the string stretched by the hanging block? (Assume that the string follows Hook's law)
94113.sol:
Since the mass of the string is small compared to the mass $m$ , the tension force is approximately constant

$∴ T = mg$

$kx = mg, x = \dfrac{mg}{k}$

$x = 2L$ given

Where $L -$ Relaxed length.

$Newlength = 2L$

$= \dfrac{2mg}{k}$

$∴$ mass per unit length

$µ = \dfrac{mk}{2mg} = \dfrac{k}{2g}$

Speed of wave $V = \sqrt{\dfrac{T}{\mu}}$

$= \sqrt{\dfrac{mg \times 2mg}{mk}}$

$V = g\sqrt{\dfrac{2m}{k}}$

$time = \dfrac{2L}{V}$

$= \dfrac{2mg}{k} \times \dfrac{1}{g}\sqrt{\dfrac{k}{2m}}$

$time = \sqrt{\dfrac{2m}{k}}$

94150.text: A simple harmonic wave of amplitude$8$unit travels along the positive x-axis. At given instant of time, for a particle at a distance of $10$ cm from the origin, the displacement is $+ 6$ unit and for a particle at a distance of $25$ cm from the origin, the displacement is $+ 4$unit. options:

$210$ cm

$250$ cm

$Y = Asin ⁡ \dfrac{2\pi}{\lambda} \left(vt - x\right)$

$\dfrac{Y}{A} =$ sin ⁡ 2\pi $\left(\dfrac{t}{T} - \dfrac{x}{\lambda}\right)$

In first case, $\dfrac{{Y}_{1}}{A} = sin ⁡ 2\pi \left(\dfrac{t}{T} - \dfrac{{x}_{1}}{\lambda}\right)

Here, ${Y}_{1} = + 6, A = 8, {x}_{1} = 10cm$

\dfrac{6}{8} =$ sin ⁡ 2$\pi \left(\dfrac{t}{T} - \dfrac{10}{\lambda}\right) .... (i)

Similarly in the second case,

\dfrac{4}{8} =$ sin ⁡ $2\pi \left(\dfrac{t}{T} - \dfrac{25}{\lambda}\right) ... ($ ii)

From equation (i),

$2 \pi \left(\dfrac{t}{T} - \dfrac{10}{λ}\right) = {sin}^{- 1}⁡ \left(\dfrac{6}{8}\right) =0.85rad$

$⇒\dfrac{t}{T} - \dfrac{10}{\lambda} =0.14$ .... (iii)

Similarly from equation (ii),

$2\pi\left(\dfrac{t}{T} - \dfrac{25}{λ}\right) = {sin}^{- 1}⁡ \left(\dfrac{4}{8}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{6}rad$

$⇒ \dfrac{t}{T} = \dfrac{25}{λ} +0.08$ .... (iv)

Subtracting equation (iv) from equation (iii), we get

$\dfrac{15}{\lambda} =0.06$

$⇒ \lambda = 250cm$

97018.subject: Botany
97018.text: Which one of the following diagrams represents the placentation in Dianthus?
97018.sol:
Placentation is the arrangement of the ovules in the ovary and their attachment to it. Placentation are of various type in the angiosperms - marginal, axile, central, parietal, basal, and free central.

Dianthus and Primrose display free-central placentation and in it the ovules are attached at the central axis of the ovary without any septa present like in axile pattern.

In marginal placentation, ovules are attached to the ridge formed on the ventral suture of the ovary. Pea plant has this arrangement. In parietal, the ovules are attached to the inner wall or towards the periphery of the ovary, observed in mustard plant and even Argemone and poppy. Sunflower and marigold show basal placentation where the ovules are attached at the base of the ovary.

100706.subject: Physics
100706.text: A block of mass $5 \text{ kg}$ is in contact with the inner wall of a hollow cylindrical drum of radius $2 \text{ m}$. The coefficient of static friction between the block and the inner wall is $0.5$. The cylinder is vertical and rotates about its axis at an angular velocity of $2\sqrt{10} \text{ rad s}^{-1}$. What is the magnitude of the frictional force acting on the block? (Take $g = 10 \text{ m s}^{-2}$)
100706.sol:
The normal force acting on the block provides the necessary centripetal force:
$N = m\omega^2 R$
$N = 5 \times (2\sqrt{10})^2 \times 2 = 5 \times 40 \times 2 = 400 \text{ N}$

The maximum possible static friction (limiting friction) is:
$f_{max} = \mu N = 0.5 \times 400 = 200 \text{ N}$

The downward gravitational force on the block is its weight:
$W = mg = 5 \times 10 = 50 \text{ N}$

Since the required upward force to keep the block stationary ($50 \text{ N}$) is less than the maximum available static friction ($200 \text{ N}$), the block will not slip.

Static friction is self-adjusting and will only act with the magnitude necessary to balance the applied forces. Therefore, the actual frictional force acting on the block is exactly equal to its weight, which is $50 \text{ N}$.

Answer: $50 \text{ N}$

100915.subject: Physics
100915.text: A simple pendulum has a string of length $2\text{ m}$ and a bob of mass $m$. The bob is released from rest when the string is horizontal. At the lowest point of its path, the bob strikes a stationary heavy block and loses $50\%$ of its kinetic energy in the collision. The maximum angle the string makes with the vertical during the subsequent rebound is:
100915.sol:
Let the length of the pendulum be $L = 2\text{ m}$.

When released from the horizontal position, the initial height of the bob relative to the lowest point is $h_{1} = L$.
By conservation of mechanical energy, the kinetic energy of the bob just before impact at the lowest point is:
$K_{1} = mgL$

During the collision, the bob loses $50\%$ of its kinetic energy. The kinetic energy remaining just after the collision is:
$K_{2} = K_{1} - 0.5K_{1} = 0.5K_{1} = 0.5mgL$

Let $h_{2}$ be the maximum height reached by the bob during the rebound. Equating the remaining kinetic energy to the potential energy at this height:
$mgh_{2} = 0.5mgL$
$h_{2} = 0.5L$

From the geometry of a simple pendulum, the height $h$ reached when the string makes an angle $\theta$ with the vertical is given by $h = L(1 - \cos\theta)$.

Substituting $h_{2} = 0.5L$ into the geometric relation:
$0.5L = L(1 - \cos\theta)$
$0.5 = 1 - \cos\theta$
$\cos\theta = 0.5$

Therefore, the maximum angle is $\theta = 60^{\circ}$.

Answer: $60^{\circ}$

102067.subject: Physics
102067.text: An ideal gas is taken from state 1 to state 2 through a process represented by a straight line on a Pressure (P) versus Volume (V) diagram. The coordinates $(V, P)$ of state 1 are $(10 \text{ L}, 20 \text{ kPa})$ and of state 2 are $(30 \text{ L}, 60 \text{ kPa})$. If the heat supplied to the gas during this process is $2000 \text{ J}$, what is the change in its internal energy?
102067.sol:
The work done by the gas is the area under the P-V graph from state 1 to state 2. Since the process is represented by a straight line, the area under the curve forms a trapezium.

Work done, $\Delta W = \dfrac{1}{2} \times (P_1 + P_2) \times (V_2 - V_1)$

Given $P_1 = 20 \text{ kPa}$, $P_2 = 60 \text{ kPa}$, $V_1 = 10 \text{ L}$, and $V_2 = 30 \text{ L}$.

$\Delta W = \dfrac{1}{2} \times (20 + 60) \times 10^3 \text{ Pa} \times (30 - 10) \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}^3$

$\Delta W = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 80 \times 20 \text{ J} = 800 \text{ J}$

According to the first law of thermodynamics:

$\Delta Q = \Delta U + \Delta W$

Given the heat supplied to the system, $\Delta Q = 2000 \text{ J}$.

$2000 \text{ J} = \Delta U + 800 \text{ J}$

$\Delta U = 1200 \text{ J}$

Answer: $1200 \text{ J}$

103675.subject: Physics
103675.text: According to the Bohr model of a hydrogen atom, an electron revolves around the nucleus in circular orbits. What is the ratio of the magnetic dipole moment of the electron in the ground state ($n=1$) to its magnetic dipole moment in the first excited state ($n=2$)?
103675.sol:
The magnetic dipole moment of an electron revolving in the $n^{\text{th}}$ orbit of a hydrogen atom is given by $M = \dfrac{evr}{2}$.

In the Bohr model, the velocity of the electron $v \propto \dfrac{1}{n}$ and the radius of the orbit $r \propto n^2$.

Therefore, the magnetic moment $M \propto \left(\dfrac{1}{n}\right)(n^2) = n$.

Alternatively, the magnetic moment is an integral multiple of the Bohr magneton: $M = n\left(\dfrac{eh}{4\pi m_e}\right)$, which directly shows $M \propto n$.

For the ground state ($n=1$) and the first excited state ($n=2$), the ratio of their magnetic dipole moments is $\dfrac{M_1}{M_2} = \dfrac{1}{2}$, or $1:2$.

Answer: $1:2$

105606.subject: Physics
105606.text: A stationary radioactive nucleus of mass $M$ undergoes alpha decay, emitting an alpha particle of mass $m$. What is the ratio of the de-Broglie wavelength of the emitted alpha particle to that of the recoiling daughter nucleus?
105606.sol:
According to the law of conservation of linear momentum, the initial momentum of the stationary nucleus is zero. Therefore, the final momentum of the system must also be zero.

Let $\vec{p}_\alpha$ be the momentum of the emitted alpha particle and $\vec{p}_{\text{recoil}}$ be the momentum of the recoiling daughter nucleus. Applying momentum conservation:
$\vec{p}_\alpha + \vec{p}_{\text{recoil}} = 0 \implies |\vec{p}_\alpha| = |\vec{p}_{\text{recoil}}|$

The de-Broglie wavelength of a particle is given by the relation $\lambda = \dfrac{h}{p}$, where $p$ is the magnitude of its momentum.

Since the magnitudes of the momenta of the alpha particle and the recoiling daughter nucleus are exactly equal, their de-Broglie wavelengths must also be equal, regardless of their masses or kinetic energies.

Thus, the ratio $\lambda_\alpha : \lambda_{\text{recoil}} = 1 : 1$.

Answer: $1 : 1$

105612.subject: Physics
105612.text:
When light of frequency $1.5 \times 10^{15}$ Hz illuminates a metal surface, the maximum kinetic energy of the emitted photoelectrons is $2.07$ eV. Which of the following incident wavelengths will not cause photoelectric emission from this metal?
(Take $h = 4.14 \times 10^{-15}$ eV s and $c = 3 \times 10^8$ m/s)
105612.sol:
First, calculate the energy of the incident photons for the initial light source:
$E = h\nu$
$E = (4.14 \times 10^{-15} \text{ eV s}) \times (1.5 \times 10^{15} \text{ Hz}) = 6.21$ eV

Using Einstein's photoelectric equation, find the work function ($\Phi$) of the metal:
$K_{\text{max}} = E - \Phi$
$\Phi = E - K_{\text{max}}$
$\Phi = 6.21 \text{ eV} - 2.07 \text{ eV} = 4.14$ eV

Next, determine the threshold wavelength ($\lambda_0$) for this metal:
$\lambda_0 = \dfrac{hc}{\Phi}$
$\lambda_0 = \dfrac{4.14 \times 10^{-15} \times 3 \times 10^8}{4.14}$ m
$\lambda_0 = 3 \times 10^{-7}$ m $= 300$ nm

For photoelectric emission to take place, the incident wavelength must be less than or equal to the threshold wavelength ($\lambda \le \lambda_0$).
If $\lambda > 300$ nm, no emission will occur.

Among the given options, $350$ nm is greater than $300$ nm. Thus, it will not cause photoelectric emission.

Answer: $350$ nm

106433.text: Which of the following transition metal ions has a spin-only magnetic moment of $5.92 \text{ B.M.}$?
106433.sol:
The spin-only magnetic moment ($\mu$) is calculated using the formula $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)} \text{ B.M.}$, where $n$ is the number of unpaired electrons.

Given $\mu = 5.92 \text{ B.M.}$
$\sqrt{n(n+2)} = 5.92$
$n(n+2) \approx 35$
This indicates that the ion must have $n = 5$ unpaired electrons.

Let us evaluate the electronic configurations of the given ions:
$\text{Mn}^{2+} (Z=25) : [\text{Ar}] 3d^5$ ($5$ unpaired electrons)
$\text{Fe}^{2+} (Z=26) : [\text{Ar}] 3d^6$ ($4$ unpaired electrons)
$\text{Cr}^{3+} (Z=24) : [\text{Ar}] 3d^3$ ($3$ unpaired electrons)
$\text{Ni}^{2+} (Z=28) : [\text{Ar}] 3d^8$ ($2$ unpaired electrons)

Thus, $\text{Mn}^{2+}$ is the ion with $5$ unpaired electrons and a spin-only magnetic moment of $5.92 \text{ B.M.}$

Answer: $\text{Mn}^{2+}$

107007.subject: Chemistry
107007.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
107007.text:
Arrange the following elements in the decreasing order of their electronegativity:
$\mathrm{P}$, $\mathrm{S}$, $\mathrm{Cl}$, $\mathrm{O}$, $\mathrm{F}$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
107007.sol:
Electronegativity increases across a period from left to right and decreases down a group from top to bottom.

Among the given elements, $\mathrm{F}$ and $\mathrm{O}$ belong to Period 2, while $\mathrm{P}$, $\mathrm{S}$, and $\mathrm{Cl}$ belong to Period 3. Therefore, the Period 2 elements generally have higher electronegativity than the Period 3 elements.

Across Period 2, electronegativity increases from $\mathrm{O}$ to $\mathrm{F}$, so $\mathrm{F} > \mathrm{O}$.
Across Period 3, electronegativity increases from $\mathrm{P}$ to $\mathrm{Cl}$, so $\mathrm{Cl} > \mathrm{S} > \mathrm{P}$.

Combining these trends, the overall decreasing order of electronegativity is $\mathrm{F} > \mathrm{O} > \mathrm{Cl} > \mathrm{S} > \mathrm{P}$.

Placing $\mathrm{Cl}$ ahead of $\mathrm{F}$ is a common error resulting from confusing electronegativity with negative electron gain enthalpy.

Answer: $\mathrm{F} > \mathrm{O} > \mathrm{Cl} > \mathrm{S} > \mathrm{P}$

107765.subject: Chemistry
107765.text: Assuming Lewis structures that strictly obey the octet rule for second-period elements, in which of the following chemical species does the central atom have a formal charge of zero?
107765.sol:
The formal charge (FC) is calculated as $FC = V - L - \dfrac{S}{2}$.

Let us evaluate the central atom for each species assuming octet-compliant Lewis structures:

For $O_{3}$ (ozone):
The central oxygen is bonded to two other oxygen atoms (one single bond, one double bond) and has $1$ lone pair.
$FC = 6 - 2 - \dfrac{6}{2} = +1$

For $NO_{3}^{-}$ (nitrate ion):
The central nitrogen forms $4$ bonds (one double bond, two single bonds) and has $0$ lone pairs.
$FC = 5 - 0 - \dfrac{8}{2} = +1$

For $N_{3}^{-}$ (azide ion):
The central nitrogen forms $4$ bonds (two double bonds) and has $0$ lone pairs.
$FC = 5 - 0 - \dfrac{8}{2} = +1$

For $NO_{2}^{-}$ (nitrite ion):
The central nitrogen is bonded to two oxygen atoms (one single bond, one double bond) and has $1$ lone pair.
$FC = 5 - 2 - \dfrac{6}{2} = 0$

Thus, the central atom in $NO_{2}^{-}$ has a formal charge of zero.

Answer: $NO_{2}^{-}$
